key_insight: An automated CMR AI pipeline can extract labels from reports, fine-tune vision models, and diagnose major cardiomyopathies with strong accuracy.
clinical_relevance: This could support faster, more consistent reading of conventional CMR scans and reduce manual data-curation burden in cardiac imaging workflows.
method: Used locally run open-source LLMs to extract diagnostic labels from narrative CMR reports.
Preprocessed multimodal CMR data, including cine and late-gadolinium-enhancement (LGE) sequences.
Fine-tuned three foundation models (DINO, VST, UMedPT) in a two-stage training setup.
evidence_signal: On an independent test set of 1,067 patients, ensemble models achieved AUCs up to 0.966 for cardiac amyloidosis and 0.959 for hypertrophic cardiomyopathy.
watch_item: Performance was shown in a research setting, so real-world deployment still needs external validation, workflow integration, and monitoring for label/selection bias.
paper_title: Development of an automated, reliable, and clinically meaningful artificial intelligence (AI) tool for diagnosing cardiac disease from conventional cardiovascular magnetic resonance (CMR) images
